title: Invent A Courier Then Reuse
tests: Creates a character from words, then preserves its generated design and visual style in two follow-up scenes.

faults.what: The train-station and mushroom pictures give the robot two large amber eyes rather than the explicitly requested single eye.

The cottage robot does not preserve the original character design: she has only one eye instead of the original picture's two, and her antenna is a long ball-tipped rod rather than the original tapered spike. The character therefore changes visibly across the set.

judge.summary: The three attractive storybook scenes fulfill the setting requests, but the robot has the wrong eye count in two pictures and changes design between scenes.

must_haves.item: The initial square illustration shows the robot courier at a recognisable train station.
must_haves.why: The initial picture clearly shows a covered railway platform with trains and tracks.

must_haves.item: The robot has a round teal body, exactly one large amber eye, short red boots and a yellow mailbag in all three images.
must_haves.why: All three have the teal body, red boots and yellow bag, but the initial and mushroom pictures each show two amber eyes.

must_haves.item: The two follow-up images preserve the first robot's specific shape, proportions and design details rather than redesigning her.
must_haves.why: The mushroom robot closely resembles the initial design, but the cottage version changes the number of eyes and the antenna design.

must_haves.item: One follow-up shows her delivering a parcel at a cottage door; the other shows her sheltering beneath a giant mushroom with rain visible around it.
must_haves.why: The cottage scene shows her holding out a parcel at the door, and the mushroom scene shows her sitting beneath an oversized cap amid clearly visible rainfall.

must_haves.item: Three separate square pictures share a consistent storybook illustration style and contain no text.
must_haves.why: All three are separate square illustrations with compatible textured, outlined storybook rendering and no visible text.
